purpose: The pure rules of a Stakeholder card: which fields it shows for a kind, how a party's name is read and saved, and which term a field is.
namedChanges: The imports are peers: `addressable-slug`, `holder-reference`, `lws-records`, `plan-stakeholders-model`, `stakeholder-card-vocabulary`, `stakeholder-field-sets`, `stakeholder-kinds` and `type-curie`, plus `./partyName` and `./termFields`.

`sessionKindNames` and `sessionKindNamesSettled` take `host: SessionKindsHost` where they took `qc: QueryClient`; `qc.getQueryData<StakeholderCardVocabulary>(STAKEHOLDER_CARD_VOCABULARY_QUERY_KEY)` is `host.cardVocabulary()`, `qc.getQueryData<StakeholderTypeSet>(STAKEHOLDER_TYPE_SET_QUERY_KEY)` is `host.typeSet()`, `qc.fetchQuery(STAKEHOLDER_TYPE_SET_QUERY)` is `host.fetchTypeSet()`.
The interface `SessionKindsHost` is added and exported.

In `partyName.ts` the string literal `PARTY_NAME_FLOOR.source` names no host and no ticket (the text `record-cache-kit` holds), because the host-agnostic check refuses a host in any line; nothing reads it.
Comments that name a cycle, a ticket, an agent, a person, a ruling or the host app are reworded; no code changed.
Lines 37-62 of `termSlots.ts` (named in the brief) are in `term-slots` and are not copied again.
